cards.front: Recall a key point about Joints and Movement
cards.back: A joint is where two or more bones meet. Most joints in the body allow movement, and these are called synovial joints .

cards.front: What should you know about hinge joint?
cards.back: Allows movement in one plane only - flexion and extension. Like a door hinge, it opens and closes in one direction.

cards.front: What should you know about ball-and-socket joint?
cards.back: Allows movement in all three planes - the rounded head of one bone fits into the cup-shaped socket of another. This allows the widest range of movement of any joint type.

cards.front: What should you know about key concept?
cards.back: The type of joint determines which movements are possible. Hinge joints only allow flexion and extension (sagittal plane). Ball-and-socket joints allow all types of movement including rotation and circumduction.

cards.back: 1. For Joints and Movement questions, use subject-specific terminology precisely 2. Support every point with specific evidence or examples 3. For longer answers, plan your response to address all parts of the question
Fibrous outer sleeve surrounding the joint (e.g. Encloses and protects the joint; holds bones together)
Thick, stringy fluid inside the joint cavity (e.g. Lubricates the joint, reducing friction; nourishes cartilage; absorbs shock)
Smooth, tough tissue covering the ends of bones (e.g. Reduces friction between bones; absorbs shock and impact)
Inner layer of the capsule that secretes fluid (e.g. Produces synovial fluid to keep the joint lubricated)
Tough, fibrous bands connecting bone to bone (e.g. Hold bones together; restrict excessive or abnormal movement)
Fibrous cords connecting muscle to bone (e.g. Transmit the force from muscle contraction to move the bone)
Small fluid-filled sacs near the joint (e.g. Reduce friction between tendons, ligaments and bones)

cards.front: What does Range of movement mean?
cards.back: One plane only (e.g. All three planes)
Flexion and extension only (e.g. Flexion, extension, abduction, adduction, rotation, circumduction)
